business_problem: SRS resources are finite and were historically allocated through fixed rules, limiting the network’s ability to adapt resource allocation to changing demand, especially during peak hours.
solution_summary: T-Mobile is trialing AI-Managed Beamforming at newly activated New York City sites using live network traffic. Phones send Sounding Reference Signals (SRS), which provide information about radio paths affected by buildings, movement, distance, and interference; T-Mobile’s live network data is also used to train and tune a supervised-learning model. The model runs directly on Ericsson’s optimized RAN compute and silicon, predicts where demand is rising, and dynamically shifts finite SRS resources toward areas with greater expected impact. The network then uses that allocation to schedule traffic, aim beams, coordinate antennas, manage power, and tune connections, improving service during peak demand. The source describes radio-data input, model processing, and network-side use, but does not identify a separate storage layer or downstream software integration.
